key_insight: This study shows that multilingual machine learning can accurately distinguish nonfluent/agrammatic from logopenic primary progressive aphasia in Catalan-Spanish bilinguals using connected speech features from either language.
clinical_relevance: The approach could help reduce the time and language-barrier burden of aphasia subtype assessment in bilingual patients, supporting more accessible and scalable speech-based screening.
method: 34 Catalan-Spanish simultaneous bilingual patients were asked to describe a standard picture in both dominant and non-dominant languages.
Researchers extracted speech-timing, word-level, linguistic, and image-text congruence features from recorded speech.
Classification models and ensemble models were trained to separate nfvPPA from lvPPA and compared across languages.
evidence_signal: The best models reached macro-F1 scores of 93% for word-level features in the non-dominant language and 92% for ensemble modeling in the dominant language, with no significant performance difference between languages.
watch_item: This is a small single-cohort study, so external validation in larger and more diverse bilingual populations is needed before routine implementation.
paper_title: Differentiating nonfluent/agrammatic and logopenic primary progressive aphasia in Catalan-Spanish bilinguals by applying multilingual multimodal machine learning to connected speech
